assertions.name: saturation_regime_unreachable_in_the_nuclear_chart
assertions.source: coth within 10% of its limit needs A = 444.26121; heaviest known nuclide is A = 294.

assertions.name: hypothesis_spread_is_of_order_the_scatter
assertions.source: The separation the test achieved, in units of the noise it is judged against: max spread 4.897% = 1.38703x the 3.531% scatter. A gap of order the noise is not a discrimination.

description: Reachability check on the kappa(A) discrimination test (bean qou-i6rg), asking the prior question: does the measured series reach the regime in which its hypotheses diverge? Computed entirely from the contest's own fitted constants and the committed series -- no new hypothesis, nothing scored, nothing fitted. Also records a second, O2-independent route to the same kernel subtraction: on H^3 the Green's function normalised to vanish at infinity is -(coth(r) - 1)/4pi, so the saturating form is the non-decaying choice of the additive constant.

alpha_range_spanned.note: H_coth's own bound-only fitted scale, taken from the committed contest rather than refitted here.

saturation_onset.criterion: coth(alpha) within the given tolerance of its limit 1
saturation_onset.reading: Saturation is the feature the discrimination test was built to detect. If the A it requires lies beyond the nuclear chart, the test cannot be run -- which is a different and stronger statement than the test having been run and come out close.

separability_from_short_range_asymptotic.reading: Over the measured range coth(alpha) = 1/alpha + alpha/3 - alpha^3/45 + ... If coth cannot be told apart from that short-range expansion at the scatter the contest uses, then whatever advantage H_coth has on this data comes from the curvature term alpha^2/3, NOT from saturation.

separation_achieved_vs_scatter.reading: The predictive gap the two hypotheses actually open across the measured series, in units of the scatter they are judged against. A gap of order 1 scatter is not a discrimination.

independent_route_to_the_subtraction.claim: The decaying Green's function of H^3 is -(coth(r) - 1)/4pi, not -coth(r)/4pi.
independent_route_to_the_subtraction.why: The radial Laplacian on H^3 is u'' + 2 coth(r) u', so harmonic solutions off the origin are -C coth(r) + D. C is fixed by the delta normalisation; D is fixed by the boundary condition. Requiring decay at infinity gives D = C, i.e. coth(r) - 1 ~ 2 e^(-2r). The saturating form is D = 0, which does not decay.
independent_route_to_the_subtraction.significance: This reaches the same subtraction as the O2 finding by a route that needs neither compactness nor finite volume, so the two are independent.
independent_route_to_the_subtraction.poincare_series: For finite covolume Gamma the critical exponent is delta = 2 and #{d <= R} ~ c e^(2R), which exactly cancels the e^(-2R) decay, so the Green's-function Poincare series diverges. That divergence is O2 in analytic form: no Green's function exists on a finite-volume quotient without the -1/vol(M) source correction. Standard; stated, not re-derived, and nothing here rests on it.

scope.class: (a) scope-limited negative on a TEST, not on a hypothesis
scope.what_is_claimed: The A = 63 series does not reach the regime in which its hypotheses diverge, so it cannot have selected among them on the stated grounds.
scope.what_is_NOT_claimed: That H_coth is false, that a power law is true, or that the metric Coulomb route fails. This is about what the measurement can resolve, not about which kernel is right. Nothing is wired.

data.verdict: The series spans alpha in [0.28773, 0.79382]. Saturation to within 10% of the limit needs alpha = 1.5222612, i.e. A = 444.26121 -- BEYOND the heaviest known nuclide (A = 294), so the discriminating regime is not reachable in any nucleus, let alone in this series. Over the measured range coth is within 0.6928% of its two-term short-range expansion 1/alpha + alpha/3, against the 3.531% scatter the hypotheses are judged on. And the two hypotheses' predictions differ by at most 4.897% across the whole series = 1.387x that scatter. So bean qou-i6rg's 'measurement that selects the hyperbolic kernel or kills it' could not have done either: what H_coth's advantage tracks on this data is the short-range curvature term, not the saturation the test was named for.
